title: Mechanisms, subsystems, container
summary: How a real robot's code is organized.

say.never: A real robot's code is organized in three layers, and each has one job. At the bottom, a **mechanism** knows how to run one device (spin a wheel at a speed). In the middle, a **subsystem** decides *when* ("the button is held, so spin up"). At the top, the **container** keeps a list of all the subsystems.

board.code:
RobotContainer        // lists every subsystem
  ShooterSubsystem     // decides: when the button's held, spin up
    FlywheelMech       // knows how to spin a wheel at a speed
    RollerMech         // knows how to run a roller

say.never: You've already used one! The drivetrain was a mechanism the whole time. In this lesson we wrap it in a subsystem, then build a brand-new shooter next to it.
say.bit: The drivetrain was a mechanism all along. This lesson wraps it in a subsystem and builds a shooter next to it.

say.never: Read the drivetrain subsystem first. Hold down **Ctrl** and tap **P**. A small search box pops up at the top. Type `DrivetrainSubsystem`, then press **Enter**. It finds any file by its name, so you never have to dig through folders.
say.bit: Read the drivetrain subsystem first. Press **Ctrl+P**, type `DrivetrainSubsystem` and press Enter. Quick Open finds any file by name, so you never have to dig through folders.

say.never: Find the teleop state. Click in the code, then hold **Ctrl** and tap **F** to open the search box. Type `case ARCADE` and press **Enter**. The editor scrolls to the right spot and highlights it.
say.bit: Find the teleop state. Press **Ctrl+F**, type `case ARCADE` and press Enter to jump to it.

say.never: When the drivetrain is in the `ARCADE` state, it drives using the sticks. The line is `drive.arcadeDrive(OI.getForward(), OI.getTurn());`. You'll write it in a moment.
say.bit: In the ARCADE state, drive with `drive.arcadeDrive(OI.getForward(), OI.getTurn());`.
